items.title: Library supplement: Sum of coordinate divergences

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n,N\), every family \(V_i:M_{n,N}\to E_n\), and every configuration \(x\), sum the total sphere divergences of the sections \(y\mapsto V_i(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). There is no factor \(1/N\); for \(N=0\) the sum is zero. No regularity or tangency is part of the definition. The ordinary product Riemannian divergence interpretation applies to jointly C¹ components satisfying pointwise tangency. The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(G:S_n\to E_n\), define \(G^{\mathrm r}(z)=G(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(G^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\operatorname{div}_S^{\mathrm{tot}}G(u)=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)}\operatorname{deriv}_{\mathrm{tot}}[t\mapsto(G^{\mathrm r}(u+t e_j))_j](0)\). Here \(e_j\) is the standard Euclidean coordinate vector, and each total scalar derivative is the ordinary derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Pointwise tangency means \(V_i(x)\perp x_i\) for every \(i,x\); joint C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.
assumptions: Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.
